I have been farming this same land in Quzhou my whole life. My children have moved to Shijiazhuang and Tianjin for work. It is just me now, managing the plot my family has always worked. My back is not what it was, but I know this land.

I will grow winter wheat and summer maize, same rotation as always, same as my neighbors, same as my mother did. Four mu is what I can handle alone anymore. I tried growing cotton once, years ago — too much work. Wheat and maize, I know. I do not need to think hard about it.

For the wheat, I will buy the same improved seed from the village supply shop — I do not remember the variety name but I always get the same bag as last year, it does well. I will rotary till before sowing, apply the compound fertilizer at planting and urea in spring when the green returns. I irrigate four times: once before sowing to settle the soil, once before the ground freezes, once when jointing starts, once at heading. I spray herbicide in winter and one more time near harvest for aphids if they come.

For the maize after wheat harvest, I will use the hybrid seed everyone uses — Xianyu or similar, the shop recommends it every year. I sow directly into the stubble without tilling to save my knees and the fuel cost. Rain comes more in summer, so I only irrigate twice, once at planting if it is dry, once at silking. Two pesticide sprays, one early for fall armyworm, one mid-season.
